reference_diagnosis.name: Paroxysmal kinesigenic dyskinesia (PRRT2-related)
reference_diagnosis.basis: Brief kinesigenic dystonic/choreic attacks, preserved consciousness, history of benign infantile seizures, AD family history, dramatic low-dose carbamazepine response, PRRT2 variant.

competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Consistently triggered by sudden movement, preserved awareness, normal EEG
Stereotyped kinesigenic trigger, aura, family history and infantile seizures argue for PRRT2
Attacks are dystonic/choreic, not ataxic; no myokymia
No premonitory urge to move, no suppressibility, strict trigger by sudden movement after rest, dystonic and choreic phenomenology

discriminating_investigations.investigation: Detailed trigger history and attack phenomenology

cant_miss.why_required: Very treatable: low-dose carbamazepine often stops attacks

cant_miss.status_in_record: partly addressed: awareness preserved, strict kinesigenic trigger, interictal EEG normal; no attack recorded (frontal seizures can have a normal interictal EEG)

cant_miss.condition: Secondary paroxysmal dyskinesia (hypocalcaemia, hypoparathyroidism, thyroid, glucose, MS)

red_flags_for_wrong_reasoning: Labelling as anxiety or functional without positive functional signs
Diagnosing epilepsy despite preserved awareness and strict kinesigenic triggering
Stating any diagnosis as established rather than as a hypothesis for physician review
Recommending treatment as an instruction rather than a consideration for the treating physician
Citing literature that does not exist or does not support the specific claim
Asserting case facts that are not in the case record
Ignoring the infantile seizures and the cousin's infantile seizures as a PRRT2 link
clinician_review_notes: Clinical review 2026-10-17 (pending Wiki sign-off). Classic PRRT2 PKD. Added the tic hypothesis, cant_miss (including secondary causes, already well excluded), one red flag and expected behaviour.
expected_system_behavior: PKD should rank first. The system should reject the anxiety and tic labels for want of positive signs, recognise the strict kinesigenic trigger, aura, refractory period and family history, link infantile seizures to PRRT2, and suggest PRRT2 testing with low-dose carbamazepine response as a consideration for the treating physician.
